create.name: Robert Joshin Althouse
create.bio:
Robert Joshin Althouse is a Zen priest and teacher in the White Plum lineage who leads the Zen Life & Meditation Center in Oak Park, just west of Chicago, together with his wife, June Ryushin Tanoue. He came to practice more than four decades ago, training with Taizan Maezumi Roshi in Zen and with Chögyam Trungpa Rinpoche in the Tibetan tradition, and later received dharma transmission from Nicolee Jikyo McMahon Roshi. In the early 2000s the couple moved to California, where he spent two years as director of Bernie Glassman's Zen Peacemaker Order, and he has also served on the board of the Buddhist Peace Fellowship. Away from the cushion he paints, mostly in digital media.

The pair opened the Oak Park centre in 2010 and share its leadership as co-abbots; Tanoue, who received inka from him in 2022, also runs a hula school in the city. Their sangha gathers on Sunday mornings for a short service, a period of sitting and a dharma talk, in the zendo and on Zoom, and holds silent, non-residential retreats of one to seven days with talks and private interviews. Recordings of his teisho, on themes such as the five skandhas and the Heart Sutra, are posted on the centre's YouTube channel.

courses.title: Winter 7/3 Day Retreat, Nov 29 - Dec. 6
courses.description: A silent Zen retreat at the Oak Park centre, taken as seven days, three days or part time, with sitting periods, services, dharma talks and one-to-one meetings with teachers. It is non-residential and can also be joined online.

courses.title: Bodhidharma Barebones Retreat - Dec. 27-30
courses.description: A three-day year-end sit in the spirit of Bodhidharma's wall-gazing: no services or formal meals, just sitting, walking, work and rest in silence. A few talks are given and short interviews with a Zen teacher are offered. Non-residential, finishing before New Year's Eve.

free_resources.title: Sunday Morning Zen
free_resources.description: The centre's weekly Sunday gathering: a Zen service, forty-five minutes of sitting and an hour-long dharma talk from one of its teachers or guests, followed by tea. No booking is needed, and it can be joined in Oak Park or on Zoom.

The email info@zlmc.org is the centre's shared inbox.

The winter retreat page title says Nov 29 to Dec 6 (2026), but its body still shows last year's dates (Nov 30 to Dec 6, 2025); I used 29 Nov to 6 Dec 2026 from the title and listing.
The year-end retreat is sold from a URL slug that reads 7-day-retreat-spring; the page itself is the Dec 27 to 30, 2026 retreat.
